lines.speaker: MOM
lines.text: Did you finish your homework?

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Yep.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Something in your spine goes... pop.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Your hoodie gets tighter. Your voice drops.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And there's a hair on your chin that wasn't there a second ago.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: You were fifteen.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Now, you're sixteen.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Because in this world, every time you lie, you get one year older.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Not your mind. Just your body. Instantly.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And it never goes back.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: That sounds easy to avoid. Until you do the math.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: In one study, researchers asked a thousand American adults how many lies they'd told in the last twenty four hours.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: The average was one point six five a day.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: At that rate, a fifteen year old would be ninety in about six weeks.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: But here's the weird part.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Six out of ten people said they hadn't told a single lie that day.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And half of all the lies came from just one person in twenty.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: So the rule is simple. Be one of the six.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Day one. Your best friend Sam just got a haircut.

lines.speaker: SAM
lines.text: Be honest. Is it good?

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: It looks like... a decision.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Your teacher asks if you read chapter four. You didn't.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Detention.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Your mom made meatloaf. You say you're not that hungry.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Which is true. Because you saw the meatloaf.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And then something strange happens. People start trusting you.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Is this text too clingy? Ask Eli.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Does this shirt work? Ask Eli.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: By Friday, half the school wants your opinion.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Because you are the only person in the building who can't lie to them.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Then the lies start slipping out. Not big ones. Reflex ones.

lines.speaker: MOM
lines.text: Did you eat the last cookie?

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Pop. Seventeen.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Someone bumps you in the hallway. I'm fine.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Eighteen.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Your aunt calls. How are you? Good, thanks!

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Nineteen.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Nineteen years old. In tenth grade.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: You shave every morning. The bus driver asks for your I.D.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And at breakfast, your mom just keeps staring at you.

lines.speaker: MOM
lines.text: Honey... are you okay?

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And that's the trap. You can't say, I'm fine.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: So you say nothing at all.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: On Saturdays, you visit Grandpa Walt.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: He taught you to ride a bike. He taught you to cheat at cards.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: These days, he doesn't always remember your name.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And every Saturday, he asks the same question.

lines.speaker: GRANDPA
lines.text: Is Rosie coming today?

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Grandma Rosie died two years ago.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: The first time, you tell him the truth.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And you watch him hear it for the very first time.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: He cries like it just happened.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Because for him, it did.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: For many people with dementia, bad news doesn't stay learned.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Every time they hear it, the grief can feel brand new.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: So some caregivers choose a gentle answer instead.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: The next Saturday, he asks again.

lines.speaker: GRANDPA
lines.text: Is Rosie coming today?

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: She's on her way, Grandpa.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Pop. Twenty.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: He smiles all afternoon.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: So you make a choice. Every Saturday. One lie. One year.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Twenty one. He hums her favorite song.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Twenty five. He combs his hair for her.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Thirty. Your knees start to ache on the stairs.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Thirty six. Your mom finds a gray hair on your hoodie...

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: and it's yours.

lines.speaker: MOM
lines.text: Eli. What is happening to you?

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: You don't answer. Because the truth would sound like a lie.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Forty one.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And then, one Saturday, Grandpa doesn't ask about Rosie.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: He looks at your face. Really looks.

lines.speaker: GRANDPA
lines.text: You've got her curse.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Wait. What?

lines.speaker: GRANDPA
lines.text: Your grandmother. Every little lie, one more year.

lines.speaker: GRANDPA
lines.text: I married her at twenty. She looked forty five.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: She told him he was a great dancer. He wasn't.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: She told your mom the dog went to live on a farm.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And every night for fifty years, she told him she wasn't tired.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Every lie she ever told was for somebody else.

lines.speaker: GRANDPA
lines.text: She spent her years on us, kiddo. Don't you spend yours on me.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Then he asks you one last time.

lines.speaker: GRANDPA
lines.text: So. Tell me the truth. Is Rosie coming?

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: No, Grandpa. She's not.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: He nods. He squeezes your hand.

lines.speaker: GRANDPA
lines.text: Good. Now go live. I'll be fine.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: It's the kindest lie you've ever heard.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: You're fifteen years old. Your body is forty one.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: You can grow a full beard, but you still can't get a driver's license.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And you've never had friends who trusted you more.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: You still visit Grandpa every Saturday. You just tell him the truth now.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And somehow, it still makes him smile.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Then, at dinner, your little sister knocks a glass off the table.

lines.speaker: MOM
lines.text: Nora! Did you do that?

lines.speaker: NORA
lines.text: Nope!

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Nothing happens. You breathe out.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And then you see it.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: One gray hair. On a seven year old.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: So, would you spend a year of your life on a kind lie? Tell us in the comments.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And subscribe. Because Nora is about to learn the rules.
